The '''2026 United States Senate election in Kentucky''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Kentucky]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congressman [[Andy Barr]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former state representative [[Charles Booker (American politician)|Charles Booker]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican incumbent [[Mitch McConnell]] is not seeking an eighth term.<ref name="Schreiner">{{Cite news|last1=Schreiner|first1=Bruce|last2=Freking|first2=Kevin|date=February 20, 2025|title=Sen. Mitch McConnell won't seek reelection in 2026, ending long tenure as Republican power broker|url=https://apnews.com/article/mitch-mcconnell-senate-retirement-34c79ef12bf62d14cb71d3c393f23a83|access-date=February 20, 2025|publisher=[[The Associated Press]]}}</ref>

[[Primary elections]] were held on May 19. Endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], Barr won the Republican nomination with 60.5% of the vote over former state attorney general [[Daniel Cameron (American politician)|Daniel Cameron]]. Booker, the Democratic nominee in [[2022 United States Senate election in Kentucky|2022]], was nominated a second time, winning over Marine officer [[Amy McGrath]] (who had narrowly defeated him in the [[2020 United States Senate election in Kentucky#Democratic primary|2020]] primary for this seat).

This will be the first open Senate election in Kentucky since [[2010 United States Senate election in Kentucky|2010]]. Democrats have not won a Senate race in Kentucky since [[1992 United States Senate election in Kentucky|1992]].

== Background ==
Kentucky, a Southern state in the [[Bible Belt]], is generally considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|Republican stronghold]], having not elected a [[Kentucky Democratic Party|Democrat]] to the U.S. Senate since [[1992 United States Senate election in Kentucky|1992]]. [[Republican Party of Kentucky|Republicans]] control both U.S. Senate seats, all but two statewide executive offices, supermajorities in both houses of the [[Kentucky General Assembly]], and all but one seat in Kentucky's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] [[Kentucky's congressional delegations|delegation]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Kentucky House and Senate Republicans maintain supermajority|url=https://kaco.org/articles/kentucky-house-and-senate-republicans-maintain-supermajority/|access-date=December 5, 2024|publisher=KACO}}</ref> Democrats control both the [[Governor of Kentucky|governorship]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Kentucky|lieutenant-governorship]], which flipped from Republican control in [[2019 Kentucky gubernatorial election|2019]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Golshan|first=Tara|date=November 6, 2019|title=Democrat Andy Beshear just unseated Kentucky's Trump-loving governor|url=https://www.vox.com/policy-and-politics/2019/11/5/20949770/kentucky-governor-election-results-andy-beshear|access-date=December 5, 2024|website=Vox|language=en-US}}</ref>

McConnell was first elected in [[1984 United States Senate election in Kentucky|1984]], defeating then-incumbent [[Walter Dee Huddleston]], and was re-elected in six subsequent elections.<ref>{{Cite news|last=McCausland|first=Phil|date=November 4, 2020|title=Sen. Mitch McConnell wins another term in Kentucky, NBC News projects|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2020-election/sen-mitch-mcconnell-wins-another-term-kentucky-nbc-news-projects-n1246037|access-date=December 5, 2024|publisher=[[NBC News]]|language=en}}</ref>
